faq.metaTitle: Frequently asked questions about Spanish lessons · Spanglish
faq.metaDescription: Answers about Spanglish’s Spanish lessons: levels, lesson length, online and face-to-face formats, kids and mature learners, prices and payments, and the free first lesson.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: What people ask us most about the lessons. Can’t find your answer? Get in touch and we’ll reply.

level.q: Do I need to know any Spanish?
level.a: No. There are lessons for every level, from complete beginner to advanced.

length.a: Lessons are 70 minutes long. Online Conversation lessons are 50 minutes, and the free first lesson is 45.

includes.a: Materials to follow the lesson, a summary afterwards and homework to prepare for the next one.

teacher.a: Maribel Mayhua, a native Spanish tutor from Lima, Peru, certified to teach levels A1 to B2 and with more than 4 years of experience. She lives in Australia.

where.q: Are lessons online or face to face?
where.a: Both. Online from anywhere, and face to face on the Sunshine Coast and in Brisbane: at the tutor’s place, at a library, at a local office or at your place, depending on the format.

formats.a: Private (1-1), your own group (up to 2 people) or a local group with other people in your area. You can take a 10-week program or pay as you go.

groups.q: Are there groups I can join?
groups.a: Yes. There are 6-week and 9-week beginner groups (the latest editions ran at Maroochydore Library and WOTSO Sippy Downs) and a 10-week Online Conversation program. Dates change with each edition, so ask us about the next ones.

online.a: A 10-week program to practise conversation from home, at intermediate level: one 50-minute online lesson a week. It costs {onlineUpfront} upfront or {onlineLesson} per lesson.

kids.q: What ages are the kids lessons for?
kids.a: For girls and boys aged 6 to 13, with games, songs and visual resources.

homeschool.a: Yes. They’re ideal for home schooling families and private learners.

minors.q: If the lesson is for someone under 18, who requests it?
minors.a: Their parent or legal guardian. They fill in the form, and lessons are arranged with them.

mature.q: Isn’t it too late to learn after 65?
mature.a: Never! There are lessons for adults over 65, from beginner to advanced: online or face to face, private or with your own group.

cost.a: Group lessons start from {groupFrom} per person (the final rate depends on your group size) and the mature adults program is {matureLesson} per lesson. Private lesson prices are sent by email. All prices are in Australian dollars (AUD).

pay.a: By bank transfer. Once you’ve made it, email hello@spanglish.com.au so we can confirm it.

upfront.q: Do I have to pay everything upfront?
upfront.a: No. Pay as you go has no upfront commitment. In the mature adults program you pay {matureLesson} per lesson, or {matureUpfront} if you pay for all 10 upfront; in the 6-week and 9-week groups, the full amount upfront or {editionLesson} per lesson.

what.q: What is the free lesson like?
what.a: It’s your first lesson with Maribel: 45 minutes, online. It’s a chance to get a feel for her teaching style, and then you decide whether to continue.

who.a: Anyone who wants to start, at any age. There’s one free lesson per person.

book.a: With the form on the “Free lesson” page, or by calling 0413 178 583, Monday to Saturday, 8am to 5pm. Maribel replies personally to arrange a day and time.

cancel.q: Can I change or cancel a lesson?
cancel.a: The conditions for changing, cancelling or making up a lesson are confirmed with Maribel when you book. If you need to change a lesson, let her know as soon as possible by phone or email.

faq.contactBody: Email or call us and we’ll reply personally.

privacy.metaDescription: What the Spanglish website collects, what we use it for and how you can access or correct it.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: In plain words: what you share with us on this website, what we use it for, and how to ask us to show, correct or delete it.

body.p1: Spanglish is Maribel Mayhua’s Spanish school, with lessons on the Sunshine Coast, in Brisbane and online (Australia).
body.p2: This policy is based on the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs) in the Privacy Act 1988.

body.p1: Only what you give us. If you request a free lesson with the form: your name, your email, your phone number (if you enter it), who the lesson is for (adults, kids or mature adults), where you’d like to take lessons, the days and times that suit you, the language you’d like to learn or practise, and your message.
body.p2: If you call or email us, whatever you tell us in that call or email.

body.p1: If the lesson is for someone under 18, the form must be filled in by their parent or legal guardian. We only ask for the age group (for example, kids aged 6 to 13), not a date of birth, and lessons are arranged with the responsible adult.
To reply to your request and organise your lessons. We don’t sell your information, we don’t use it for advertising and we don’t sign you up to any newsletter.

storage.title: How it reaches us and where it is kept

body.p1: When you send the form, your details reach Spanglish by email through an email delivery service. That service and our email provider may store data on servers outside Australia.
body.p2: We keep your details only for as long as we need them to reply to you and organise your lessons.

body.p1: This website doesn’t use analytics tools or advertising cookies. It may only store a technical cookie to remember the language you choose. Our hosting provider may log technical data, such as IP addresses, for security.
You can ask to see the information we hold about you, to correct it or to have it deleted. Email us at {email} or call us on {phone}.
Contact us first and we’ll try to sort it out. If you’re not satisfied, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) at oaic.gov.au.
If we change it, we’ll publish the new version here with its date.
